messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Sev2 — GPU capacity critical in us-west-2-prod-gpu. queue_length=1250 (+300/min), backpressure causing request throttling and 5xx for some customers. Autoscaler failing to add nodes: AttachRoleTimeout + LaunchTemplateVersionMismatch observed. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/gpu-autoscale. Paginated to @alice-oncall @bob-sre @carla-enginfra. :rotating_light:

alice-oncall: ack, I'm on it. joining bridge now. starting initial triage — checking autoscaler logs and ASG state. who has permission to manually scale nodegroups?

bob-sre: I'm here. quick check: autoscaler logs show repeated error: `failed to attach IAM role: timeout waiting for instance profile association` and cloudprovider returned `LaunchTemplateVersionDoesNotMatch` for new instances. stack traces below.

carla-enginfra: I can escalate to infra. Likely cause: recent LT rollout pinned to an old AMI/profile. I'll check launch template versions and nodegroup attach role status. prepping a manual scale as fallback.

alice-oncall: customer-facing impact: inference 5xx spikes started ~1765429000, ~12% error rate for dedicated customers on route /v1/generate. ramping fallback: divert low-priority queues to hosted pool if we can get a temporary capacity. dave-custsuccess please notify impacted customers on a short timeline.

dave-custsuccess: on it. sending a brief update to impacted accounts saying we are mitigating and may apply a temporary reroute. will post the message once we confirm mitigation path.

bob-sre: logs snippet: ```
W 2024-10-03T16:02:11Z autoscaler: failed to create instance: LaunchTemplateVersionDoesNotMatch: The provided launch template version does not exist
Caused by: iam:AttachRolePolicy timeout attaching role to instance profile (attempts=6)
```

carla-enginfra: verified: ASG `rgw-prod-gpu-gg1` has LT version 3. Recent rollout pushed LT v5 but nodegroup config still references v3. New nodes request v5 and AWS rejects. Also node-role association on new instances is intermittently failing due to instance-profile propagation delay in the account. starting manual remediation steps: 1) pin ASG to LT v3 for immediate launches 2) retry attach role 3) bump retry window 4) roll forward with controlled canary.

alice-oncall: do the pin and manual scale now. if we can get +8 GPU nodes up within 10m that should drain the queue to acceptable levels. if not, we'll enable hosted fallback routing.

carla-enginfra: Running commands: ```sh
aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name rgw-prod-gpu-gg1 --launch-template "LaunchTemplateId=lt-0abc123,Version=3"
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name rgw-prod-gpu-gg1 --desired-capacity 32
```

carla-enginfra: started desired-capacity update, ASG reports activities: `Launching a new EC2 instance: i-0f1e2d3c`

bob-sre: monitoring metrics — instance init logs show attach profile retrying. If attach keeps failing, we can patch worker node bootstrap to skip strict IAM check temporarily (dangerous) or create pre-associated instances via an image with role baked in. prefer not to.

alice-oncall: agreed, prefer ASG pin + retries. emily-devex, can we open a routing fallback? small subset of traffic to hosted to protect SLOs.

emily-devex: I can flip a traffic rule in the router. prepping canary route: move 20% of low-priority inference traffic to hosted pool, 80% stays local. doing it now.

emily-devex: command: ```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","weight":{"hosted":20,"local":80},"reason":"mitigation-gpu-autoscale-fallback"}
```

emily-devex: canary in progress — metrics will show within ~30s.

alice-oncall: update on customer impact: 3 dedicated tenants showing elevated error rate; internal SLOs alerting. dave please include that in customer note. we should also open a post-incident ticket for launch template release gating.

dave-custsuccess: message drafted, sending to impacted accounts now. will include ETA: 30-45m for mitigation, note that we're routing low-priority traffic to hosted pool.

carla-enginfra: ASG now reports 6/8 new instances InService. attach role errors decreased after forcing LT version back to 3. cloud-init logs look clean. kube nodes are registering but tainting shows `node.kubernetes.io/unavailable:NoSchedule` applied by bootstrap for older images — need to clear taint to allow pods, will cordon+uncordon after patch.

bob-sre: I'm running `kubectl get nodes -o wide` — new nodes present: gpu-n-002, gpu-n-003, status Ready? Not yet. kubelet logs show `failed to enable GPU driver: module not found` on two nodes, looks like AMI mismatch.

carla-enginfra: that matches the LT mismatch theory — we pinned to an older template but some instances launched with v5 images. I'll force-replace those instances. `aws ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids i-0bad111` for the ones with wrong AMI. relaunching clean.

alice-oncall: while infra fixes, emily, bump hosted route to 40% if error doesn't drop within 5m.

emily-devex: acknowledged. bump ready.

bob-sre: error rate fell to ~3% after 20% hosted canary and 6 new nodes moved to Ready. queue length down to 420. still watching for regression.

alice-oncall: good. continuing mitigation: infra continue node replace & attach policy retries. SRE will monitor autoscaler logs and do a postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigating. Incident link: https://redwood/incidents/1765432222. Actions logged: ASG pinned to LT v3, desired-capacity increased, hosted canary routing enabled.

alice-oncall: next steps: 1) keep hosted canary until queue <200 and error rate <1% for 10m. 2) infra to complete node replacement and confirm AMI/driver consistency. 3) eng to schedule LT rollout gating & preflight checks. 4) open postmortem and customer follow-up.

dave-custsuccess: sent initial update to customers. will follow up with root-cause note after postmortem.

carla-enginfra: replacing 2 bad instances now. new nodes coming up with correct drivers. kube status improving.

bob-sre: monitoring shows steady improvement; queue 190, error rate 0.8%. keeping bridge open for 20m then hand to incident cleanup.

alice-oncall: thanks all. I'll keep monitoring and then file the incident ticket with timeline. closing pager for now but leaving thread open. :white_check_mark:
